stories.headline: Nvidia privately confirmed it could track chips to fight smuggling, even as industry publicly questioned feasibility
stories.summary: Representatives from Nvidia told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the Chip Security Act, Foster told MIT Technology Review in an interview on Thursday, even while an industry group claimed they were “potentially infeasible.” Foster, a Democrat who serves on the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, is a cosponsor of the act, which would introduce geotracking requirements to verify the location of advanced AI chips in order to prevent their smuggling to China. It is one of three chip-security bills under consideration for inclusion in the Senate’s National Defense Authorization Act, each of which is drawing renewed attention after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and reported affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
stories.why_it_matters: When the Chip Security Act was introduced, in May 2025, lawmakers said the technology to implement it existed, something Nvidia has not publicly confirmed. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in ai & machine learning.

stories.headline: Build once, run on any agent: A practical guide to agent skills
stories.summary: Skip to content Skip to sidebar / Blog Changelog Docs Customer stories Try GitHub Copilot app See what's new AI & ML Developer skills Engineering Enterprise software News & insights Open Source Security Home / AI & ML / GitHub Copilot Build once, run on any agent: A practical guide to agent skills Agent skills capture repeatable engineering work in files teams can review and reuse, while tools, project context, and permissions remain specific to the host that runs them. Andrea Griffiths·@AndreaGriffiths11 November 12, 2026 | 6 minutes Share: How many times this week did you re-explain the same task to an agent? How many times did you ask your colleague with deep institutional knowledge how to solve a specific problem? That context shouldn’t be lost in a chat or locked in one person’s head.
stories.why_it_matters: Agent skills let you capture repeatable instructions so you and your agents can reuse them. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in developers.
key_points: Problem & Context: Skip to content Skip to sidebar / Blog Changelog Docs Customer stories Try GitHub Copilot app See what's new AI & ML Developer skills Engineering Enterprise software News & insights Open Source Security Home / AI & ML / GitHub Copilot Build once, run on any agent: A practical guide to agent skills Agent skills capture repeatable engineering work in files teams can review and reuse, while tools, project context, and permissions remain specific to the host that runs them.
Technical Implementation: An agent skill is a versioned directory centered on a SKILL.md file that describes when and how to do a repeatable task.
Deployment & Impact: You can share those instructions across agents, but the environment still needs to provide the tools, credentials, and permissions to carry them out.

stories.headline: Fact-Checking at Scale: Building a More Accurate and Efficient Synopsis Factuality System
stories.summary: By Shreya S Ramanujam , Yongce Li , Afshine Amidi , Sina Ghiassian , Benjamin Klein. Introduction Picture this — you’re home after a long day at work and can’t wait to catch up on Bridgerton.
stories.why_it_matters: You log on to Netflix, search for “Bridgerton” and land on this screen: If this sounds familiar, you already know what a synopsis is — it’s a short glimpse into what a viewer can expect to see in a show. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in big tech.
key_points: Problem & Context: At Netflix’s scale, with thousands of titles, multiple episodes per season and multiple languages, fact-checking all of these by hand simply doesn’t scale.

Technical Implementation: Our current factuality checker feeds a reasoning model everything we know about a title (like metadata and text assets) and asks it to judge synopsis factuality according to a rigorous rubric.

Deployment & Impact: There are two main limitations of this approach that we want to optimize: High cost of long-context reasoning calls: Each decision requires expensive, long-context model calls to reasoning models, which doesn’t scale well when we want to check multiple titles, episodes, languages, and style variants.

On peak days, roughly 100,000 workloads fail.
stories.why_it_matters: When workloads fail, the failure itself is only the beginning. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in big tech.

Deployment & Impact: Even a small share of difficult failures can consume engineering time, waste compute, and interrupt critical data pipelines.

stories.headline: Zugwise: Domain-Aware Game Reconstruction for Digitizing Handwritten Chess Scoresheets
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.14544v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Digitizing handwritten chess scoresheets has been studied as a handwriting-recognition problem: read the move in each box and check that it is legal. This framing misses the errors that matter most.
stories.why_it_matters: A misread that yields an illegal move is loud. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in technology research.
key_points: Problem & Context: Two learned signals, CTC re-scoring against the recognizer's raw output and a Maia-style human-move prior, raise the correct fix's top-rank rate from 58.8% to 78.0% of the replacement decisions where it is a candidate, and hold without refitting on a later section.

Technical Implementation: The system runs entirely in the browser and is free, private, and offline-capable; alongside it we offer a three-way adjudication protocol for a domain where no single record is ground truth.
Deployment & Impact: A misread that yields an illegal move is loud.

stories.headline: Cleaning an Agent's History Hurts When the World Still Holds the Error
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.14654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using language-model agents accumulate histories of their own mistakes, and a system that compacts, repairs or hands off such a history decides what it says about those mistakes while their effects stay in the world. Prior work cleans the history at a fixed world, where showing a corrected step and saying it is done move together.
stories.why_it_matters: We ask whether the same correct content helps or hurts depending on how the history states it and what the world holds. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in technology research.
key_points: Problem & Context: arXiv:2611.14654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using language-model agents accumulate histories of their own mistakes, and a system that compacts, repairs or hands off such a history decides what it says about those mistakes while their effects stay in the world.
Technical Implementation: We freeze an agent mid-task with its exact world state, edit the history or the world, and let a receiver model continue.
Deployment & Impact: The note raises recovery, the share of remaining targets the receiver gets right, from 51% under a matched neutral note to 66%.
